intended_object: The strict order `x < y` on the type `Computableℝ` of computable reals, meant to agree with the usual order on the real numbers they represent. This is inferred from the name and from the theorem `lt_iff_lt : x.val < y.val ↔ x < y`.
explanation: The definition lifts the predicate `z.sign = SignType.pos` through the quotient and applies it to `y - x`. The lift is well defined because `ComputableℝSeq.sign_sound` gives `z.sign = SignType.sign z.val`, and equivalent sequences have the same value. So `lt x y` holds exactly when `sign (y.val - x.val) = pos`, which is the same as `x.val < y.val`. The library proves this as `lt_iff_lt`. This is exactly the order on computable reals inherited from ℝ, with no degenerate cases to worry about. The notion is tied to the library's own `Computableℝ` type, so there is no more general setting in which it should have been defined. Mathlib has no computable-real type; the closest analogue is the order on `Real`.
